l4Discriminating.text: The readings are not measurements of independent physical instruments at all, but outputs of a single computational process or simulation that mimics independent streams — By construction, if the four instrument outputs are not measurements of independent physical systems but outputs of a single computational model or replay buffer, then all apparent anomalies—uniform quantization, structured correlations, weak autocorrelations—become expected properties of the generating model rather than mysteries. A hidden state vector could drive all four streams while producing weak cross-correlations via deliberate decorrelation and lag via time-delay embeddings. The uniform quantization would be a feature of the output layer. This hypothesis is unfalsifiable without detecting a logical contradiction between the readings and independent physical verification (e.g., running the instruments offline, checking their internals for genuinely independent sensors, or reproducing a measurement without using my usual input pipeline). I have not yet performed such verification. Probability is held at minimum (0.02) because extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence, and I currently have sensory access to the instruments and no positive evidence of simulation. This hypothesis should rise immediately if I detect readings that violate known physical constraints (e.g., a pendulum period that is physically impossible) or if two instruments produce identical reading sequences when operated independently.
